newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CBA says rate cuts boost mortgage share.
newsitem.headline: CBA says rate cuts boost mortgage share.

text.p: Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CBA) managing director David Murray said on Wednesday that the bank's pre-emptive mortgage rate cuts in the past year had improved the bank's market share.

"Our market share continues to rise and so the difference between our position today and our position in May last year is quite significant," Murray told reporters after an address to the Committee for Economic Development of Australia (CEDA).
Cuts to Australian home loans has cut about 100 basis points off bank home lending margins.
"We have built more business then we would have otherwise and what's critical is that the business is more sustainable and more competitive than a year ago," Murray said.

Commonwealth Bank's pre-emptive rate cuts, the first in May last year and the second in February this year, had bought the major banks into line with the mortgage originators and had therefore reduced the pricing differences within the market that had forced significant churning.
